description: Interactive debugger for Dockerfile, with support for IDEs (VS Code, Emacs, Neovim, etc.)

summary.one_liner: buildg is an interactive debugger for Dockerfile builds based on BuildKit, with breakpoints, step execution, a debug shell, and DAP support for editors like VS Code, Emacs, and Neovim.
summary.what_it_does: Runs a Dockerfile build under an interactive debug session via the `buildg debug` command, showing source lines with a current-line marker. Users can set line breakpoints or an on-fail breakpoint, step to the next line, continue to a breakpoint, and list or review build logs. A debug shell (`exec`) opens a shell on a build step's rootfs so users can run their own tools, optionally using a custom image. It also provides a Debug Adapter Protocol server (`buildg dap serve`) so editors can drive the debugger. Build options include secrets, SSH forwarding, build args, target stage, and cache import/reuse. The README describes rootless support and cache management commands (prune, du).
use_cases: debug Dockerfile from VS Code or Neovim
how_to_run: Install runc (and optionally RootlessKit and slirp4netns); see the README Install section for release tarballs
git clone the repository, cd buildg, then run make
Or run in Docker: docker run --rm -it --privileged -v /path/to/ctx:/ctx:ro ghcr.io/ktock/buildg:0.4 debug /ctx
notable: Interactive debug shell on any build step, with optional custom debugger image via --image
Breakpoints on Dockerfile line numbers or on-fail, plus next/continue stepping
DAP server for editor integration (VS Code, Emacs, Neovim)
Built on BuildKit; also available as a nerdctl subcommand (nerdctl builder debug)
caveats: Early stage software; built on BuildKit with unmerged patches
Native execution only on Linux; other platforms need a Linux VM
IDE integration over DAP requires rootless execution
